parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented universal exposure (no birth-sex facility rule, no border/document friction, no police targeting), and no documented violence. Positives are documented and current: 2009 gender recognition, gender reassignment protected under the 2017 equality act, a 2024 conversion-practice ban, marriage/partner recognition, gender-neutral sexual offences law, and official reconciliation with past anti-gay enforcement. This is a well-documented jurisdiction, so the absence of recorded anti-trans incidents is moderately meaningful rather than mere silence. Deductions: prison placement and hate-crime-bill status are open questions, not exposures, but they leave custody and remedy coverage unproven; the dossier documents legal machinery more than demonstrated visitor-facing enforcement (no service audits, prosecutions of attackers, or acceptance research). Residual social friction is unrecorded but plausible. Net: reduced risk near the low-risk boundary.
